provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2022RS/bills/hb/hb0423f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed, January 19, 2022); in the text file the digit 5 is missing from the first-offense minimum in § 4-204(c) and § 4-404(b) (shown as ... in the quotes); no enrolled text was read. Also in the bill and not quoted for length: Criminal Procedure § 5-202(f) (commissioner may not authorize pretrial release for listed firearm crimes), the added prior-conviction bars in Public Safety § 5-133(c), the 5-133(b)(2) penalties, § 4-306(b) and § 5-142/5-144 penalties. Section 1 and 2 only renumber subsections. No passage vote is recorded.

Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Correctional Services § 6-101(m)): (4) absconding; OR (5) USE OR POSSESSION OF A FIREARM.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4-204(c)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and, in addition to any other penalty imposed for the crime of violence or felony, shall be sentenced: 1. FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, to imprisonment for not less than ... years and not exceeding 20 years; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 10 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4-404(b)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a felony and on conviction, IN ADDITION TO ANY OTHER PENALTY IMPOSED FOR THE CRIME OF VIOLENCE OR FELONY, is subject to: (I) FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN ... YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS; AND (II) FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 10 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 7-104(h)): A PERSON CONVICTED OF THEFT OF A FIREARM, INCLUDING AN ANTIQUE FIREARM OR A REPLICA OF AN ANTIQUE FIREARM, IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND: (I) 1. FOR A FIRST CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 2 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $2,500; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 15 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000;
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-134(c)): A DEALER OR OTHER PERSON MAY NOT SELL, RENT, LOAN, OR TRANSFER A REGULATED FIREARM TO A PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE IF THE DEALER OR OTHER PERSON HAS ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE THAT THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE: (I) WAS PREVIOUSLY CONVICTED OF: 1. A CRIME OF VIOLENCE; ... (II) INTENDS TO USE THE REGULATED FIREARM TO: 1. COMMIT A CRIME; OR 2. CAUSE HARM TO THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, TRANSFEREE, OR RECIPIENT OR ANOTHER PERSON. ... A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 15 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-138): A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SECTION IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND: (1) (I) FOR A FIRST CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 2 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $2,500;
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-141(b)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and on conviction is subject to imprisonment FOR NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS AND not exceeding 15 years AND a fine not exceeding $25,000.
